title: Cobalt Breach — Anime Mecha Episode Ident
description: A hard diagonal split separates a flat-color mecha silhouette from oversized katakana brush type, replicating the kinetic title-card grammar of classic anime OPs. Sets itself apart from glow-heavy neon templates through deliberate flat-color restraint and a corner monospace episode tag.
philosophy: This template borrows from cel-animation, not screens — it refuses gradients, lens flares, and scanline noise in favor of the two-color contrast economy that defined Gainax and Sunrise title sequences. It exists for the presenter who wants the slide to land like a punch before a single word is spoken. The diagonal is not decoration; it is the entire compositional argument. Meant for rooms where spectacle and economy of means are the same thing.
goodFor: Anime fan community keynotes and convention panels
Game or media reveal title cards needing single-image impact
Section-divider slides in a series-format deck
Event intro screens displayed before a talk begins
avoidFor: Data-heavy quarterly business reviews with multiple charts
Academic research presentations requiring dense body text
Corporate investor decks expecting restrained professionalism
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should land like a freeze-frame title card from a classic anime opening sequence — kinetic stillness rather than motion blur. Two-color flat contrast carries the entire composition: one half is dense mass, the other is declarative type, severed by a single hard diagonal that reads like a sword cut. The mood is ceremonial and punchy, the visual grammar of a chapter reveal before battle. Avoid all digital glow, gradient blending, scanline texture, lens flare, and atmospheric haze — restraint here is the spectacle.

examples.layoutNotes: Edge-to-edge full bleed with a hard diagonal rule cutting from the upper-left quadrant to the lower-right; the mecha silhouette claims and bleeds into the dark half while oversized stacked title type occupies the contrasting half. No header band or footer strip — a corner-anchored monospace episode tag sits isolated at bottom-left, outside the primary diagonal tension zone. Hierarchy operates through scale contrast alone: silhouette reads as compressed mass, title type as declaration. No gutter or softening device touches the diagonal edge.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a freeze-frame from a mecha anime interstitial — the moment the episode title locks on screen before the OP cut. Compositional rhythm is deliberately asymmetric: the diagonal wedge creates tension on the left while the content breathes against a flat open field on the right. Mood is taut and economical, like a two-color silkscreen print — no atmospheric haze, no glow, no gradients. Avoid any softness or depth illusion; every element should read as a hard, opaque shape with zero ambiguity.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with the signature hard diagonal cutting from upper-left quadrant to lower-right, dividing a narrow flat-color accent wedge (cols 1–3) from the primary content field (cols 4–12). Content zone holds a single dominant statement — oversized brush-style numeral or short phrase — anchored to the upper third, with two to three supporting lines stacked below using weight contrast alone (no rule lines). A monospace episode/section tag is pinned to the bottom-left corner outside the main grid margin. Outer margin is tight and intentional, roughly 5–6%, giving the slide a cropped, broadcast-frame quality.
